gloss: amortization; writing off; paying off (a debt)

definitions.explanation: In accounting, spreading the cost of an asset over the years it is used, or removing its remaining value from the books. Most often met in the compound {減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}.
Clearing a debt or obligation by paying it back in full. More formal than {返済|へんさい} and largely limited to financial writing.

examples.japanese: {設備|せつび}を{償却|しょうきゃく}する。
この{機械|きかい}の{償却|しょうきゃく}{期間|きかん}は{五年|ごねん}だ。
examples.english: The depreciation period for this machine is five years.

examples.japanese: {建物|たてもの}の{取得費|しゅとくひ}は、{毎年|まいとし}{少|すこ}しずつ{償却|しょうきゃく}していく。
examples.english: The acquisition cost of the building is written off little by little each year.

examples.japanese: {借金|しゃっきん}を{償却|しょうきゃく}した。
{債務|さいむ}の{償却|しょうきゃく}に{十年|じゅうねん}かかった。
examples.english: It took ten years to pay off the debt.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{利益|りえき}の{一部|いちぶ}を{借入金|かりいれきん}の{償却|しょうきゃく}に{充|あ}てた。
examples.english: The company put part of its profits toward paying off its borrowings.

notes:
A financial term written with {償|しょう} (compensate) + {却|きゃく} (dispose of). Used as a noun and with する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {減価償却|げんかしょうきゃく}: depreciation of fixed assets
- {償却|しょうきゃく}{期間|きかん}: amortization period
- {償却|しょうきゃく}{資産|しさん}: depreciable assets
- {債務|さいむ}を{償却|しょうきゃく}する: to pay off a debt

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {返済|へんさい}: repayment — the everyday word for paying back money
- {焼却|しょうきゃく}: incineration — a homophone with a completely different meaning; distinguish by context
